notification_en: ANICCA. IMPERMANENCE.
REMEMBER DEATH.
LIFE IS FLEETING.
NOTHING LASTS.
ALL THINGS PASS.
WAKE UP.
THIS BREATH MAY BE YOUR LAST.
IMPERMANENCE IS HERE.
BE PRESENT.
PRACTICE DYING.
BIRTH AND DEATH ARE A GREAT MATTER.
DO NOT BE HEEDLESS.
LIFE HANGS ON A SINGLE BREATH.
You are one breath away from the next life.
What are you waiting for?
Living or just existing?
Are you awake?
What truly matters?
How will you use today?
Have you practiced today?
Ready to die today?
Any regrets?
Who did you give your time to?
What are you avoiding?
What are you clinging to?
Were you mindful today?
Death doesn't wait.
Every second counts.
Your clock is ticking.
Closer than yesterday.
One day less.
Nothing is permanent.
All things end.
This too shall pass.
This body is only borrowed.
Form is emptiness.
You're not immortal.
Time is running out.
The end approaches.
Tomorrow isn't guaranteed.
The next breath isn't promised.
This may be the last time you meet.
Health is not a given.
You are getting older.
Everything is changing.
TICK. TOCK.
STILL ALIVE?
NOT DEAD YET.
Surprise! Still breathing.
Your expiration approaches.
DON'T SLEEP.
STOP PUTTING IT OFF.
How many times do you think you have left?
Will you scroll your life away?
NOW OR NEVER.
TODAY COULD BE IT.
LIVE BEFORE YOU DIE.
THIS IS YOUR REMINDER.
MEDITATE ON DEATH.
LET GO.
BE HERE NOW.
STOP SCROLLING. START LIVING.
Do the most important thing first.
Go see who you want to see.
Do the thing you fear but must do.
Put the phone down.
Get up. Go for a walk.
Drink water. Breathe.
Say one true thing.
Do one good deed.
Live today fully.
Use this moment well.
Care for your mind first.
Bring your attention back.
Apologize. Give thanks.
Do the one thing you've been putting off.
Start now.
Just this breath—return to the breath.
Close the app. Open your life.
You just wasted another minute.
How long since you looked at the sky?
Your future self is watching.
That thing you keep postponing? Do it.
One year from now you'll wish you started today.
You're not busy. You're distracted.
When was the last time you called them?
Stop planning. Start doing.
Your body is the only place you have to live.
Eat real food. Move your body.
How do you want to be remembered?
You already know what to do.
This is not a rehearsal.
If not now, when? If not you, who?
The graveyard is full of unfinished dreams.
Your cells are dying right now.
Entropy always wins.
You'll never be this young again.
Most of your life may already be over.
Your hourglass was flipped at birth.
The clock doesn't pause while you sleep.
Each birthday marks a countdown.
Your future is shrinking.
Time doesn't care about your plans.
Another day gone. What did you do with it?
Sunset means one less day.
Everyone you love will die.
Call your parents. They're aging too.
Every meeting could be the last.
Someone will think of you for the last time.
In three generations, you'll be forgotten.
The last person who remembers you will also die.
Your childhood home will belong to strangers.
Your excuses will die with you.
Your plans mean nothing to death.
The universe doesn't care about your deadline.
You're a guest, not an owner.
Everything you own will belong to someone else.
Your name will be said for the last time.
All empires fall. So will yours.
The pyramids are already half sand.
Write that letter.
Make the call you've been avoiding.
Go outside. Touch grass.
Look someone in the eye today.
Cook a meal. Eat slowly.
Walk without your phone.
Sit still for five minutes.
Give something away today.
Permanence is an illusion. See through it.
You are a temporary arrangement of atoms.
Life is a brief candle.
You are stardust afraid of becoming dust again.
Existence is temporary. Make it count.
This is the only moment that exists.
Social media won't attend your funeral.
Those likes won't matter on your deathbed.
Your inbox will outlive you.
WiFi cuts out. So will you.
A life fed by algorithms is no life at all.
Empty your cup.
The flower doesn't try to bloom. It just does.
The best time was yesterday. The next best is now.
Your headstone won't list your job title.
Nobody on their deathbed wished they'd worked more.
One conversation can change everything. Have it.
Listen to your heartbeat.
That person is aging too.
Some conversations won't have a next time.
The sun will burn out too.
This street might not exist in a hundred years.
You last but a moment.
Your existence is a statistical miracle.
No one will finish looking at your saved photos.
Your account will eventually be deactivated.
Your shopping cart won't follow you to the grave.
The comment section isn't life.
A hundred years later, just a stone remains.
No one will remember what you wore.
Your social media feed will become a memorial.
Your star ratings will outlive you.
Your password will become a permanent secret.
Do you remember this day last year?
Ten years from now you won't remember today.
This moment is already becoming the past.
Your childhood is already a historical record.
Even at 3 AM, the countdown continues.
You are stardust, briefly self-aware.
The ocean is four billion years older than you.
The people you follow don't know who you are.
Your search history is more honest than your diary.
Your unread messages won't wait for you.
The algorithm knows your weaknesses better than you.
Your scent will fade from your clothes.
Your favorite chair will be moved away.
Your pillow will be replaced.
Your plants will die too.
Your shoes will be put in a bag.
Your maps still save places you'll never visit again.
Your last like meant nothing.
Someone died the day you were born.
Someone on Earth is dying right now.
Your mortgage might outlive you.
The next meal isn't guaranteed.
Your brain is deleting your memories.
Spring will come after you die.
Your bookmarked articles will never be read.
Your medical reports get longer every year.
When did you last really look at the moon?
You've forgotten most of your childhood.
You will walk your most familiar road for the last time.
Some songs you'll never hear a second time.
Who did you dream about last?
Some scents you'll never smell again.
No one will watch all your videos.
The seasons you have left are numbered.
You appeared in someone's dream, then vanished.
Your last post will remain online forever.
main_en: All conditioned phenomena are like a dream, an illusion, a bubble, a shadow, like dew, or lightning. Thus should they be contemplated.
The past mind cannot be grasped, the present mind cannot be grasped, and the future mind cannot be grasped.
Form is not different from emptiness; emptiness is not different from form. Form itself is emptiness; emptiness itself is form.
Impermanent indeed are formations. They are subject to arising and vanishing. Having arisen, they cease; their calming is true happiness.
Death is certain, the time is uncertain.
All conditioned things are subject to decay. Strive on with diligence.
Life exists in the space of a single breath.
Realize that this world is impermanent, that nations are fragile and imperiled. The four great elements bring only suffering and are empty; the five aggregates are without a self.
All who are born must die; beauty must fade; the strong are overcome by sickness—none can escape.
Even Mount Sumeru will crumble when the aeon ends; even the deep, bottomless ocean will dry up.
The span of this life is not assured: the time of death lies uncertain, and like a convict led to the scaffold, you draw closer to death with each step.
If you realize the nature of impermanence, you will not be attached to anything.
I regard death as merely a change of clothes; at the moment of death, I have no fear.
The root of all dharma is mindfulness of death.
Keep death daily before your eyes. Then you will not waste your life on trivial matters.
This precious human life is extremely rare. Having obtained it, may I accomplish its great purpose.
Death is not waiting for us at the end of a long road. Death is always with us, in the marrow of every passing moment.
A man's life is like a pile of chaff or a feather on a mountain pass. The Lord of Death comes suddenly, like an avalanche or a storm.
Your life-span decreases like the shadows of the setting sun.
This life is crossed in a brief moment, but samsara is endless.
All beings are impermanent and die. Have you not heard of those who died before you? Have you not seen your own relatives pass away? Do you not notice how we grow old?

Though you cherish this illusory body with great fondness, the time of death lies uncertain. Your white hairs and wrinkles are omens of death, so it is vital to cultivate renunciation and exert yourself in the practice of Dharma.

When you keep in mind the misery of dying, it becomes clear that all activities are causes for suffering, so give them up. Cut all ties, even the smallest, and meditate in solitude on the remedy of emptiness.
Nothing whatsoever will help you at the time of death, so practice the Dharma since it is your best companion.
Life-and-death is the Great Matter. Time passes swiftly and waits for no one. Cherish every moment!
Birth and death are a great matter, and impermanence is swift.
To study the Buddha Way is to study the self. To study the self is to forget the self.
Bodhi is fundamentally without any tree; The bright mirror is also not a stand. Fundamentally there is not a single thing— Where could any dust be attracted?
Having lived through four dynasties and five emperors, witnessing the rise and fall of nations, and having endured countless hardships, I know how fleeting worldly affairs truly are.
Blossoms fill the spring branches; the full moon rests in the heart of heaven. All is complete.
Just understand that birth-and-death is itself nirvana.
Dead and buried.
Great death, then great life.
Write the word 'death' upon your forehead—then all worldly ties will naturally fall away.
Like a prisoner walking to the execution ground, each step brings us closer to death.
You could leave life right now. Let that determine what you do and say and think.
Loss is nothing else but change, and change is Nature's delight.
Think of yourself as dead. You have lived your life. Now take what's left and live it properly.
It is not that we have a short space of time, but that we waste much of it.
Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
When you kiss your child or wife, say that you kiss a mortal.
Let death and exile, and all other things that appear terrible, be daily before your eyes—but chiefly death.
Understand that you are dying daily.
To die will be an awfully big adventure.
Our dead are never dead to us until we have forgotten them.
The boundaries which divide Life from Death are at best shadowy and vague.
The cradle rocks above an abyss, and common sense tells us that our existence is but a brief crack of light between two eternities of darkness.
Cowards die many times before their deaths; the valiant never taste of death but once.
Death destroys a man: the idea of Death saves him.
The Grave's a fine and private place, but none I think do there embrace.
Do not go gentle into that good night.
Because I could not stop for Death, He kindly stopped for me.
To die, to sleep—to sleep, perchance to dream. Ay, there's the rub.
No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main.
The paths of glory lead but to the grave.
Out, out, brief candle! Life's but a walking shadow.
Death, be not proud.
When I have fears that I may cease to be.
And death shall have no dominion.
Remembering that you are going to die is the best way I know to avoid the trap of thinking you have something to lose.
No one wants to die. Even people who want to go to heaven don't want to die to get there.
Death is the only wise advisor that we have.
Death is not the opposite of life but an innate part of life.
Look again at that dot. On it, everyone you love, everyone you know, everyone you ever heard of, every human being who ever was, lived out their lives.
The idea of death, the fear of it, haunts the human animal like nothing else; it is the mainspring of human activity.
As you read this, cells in your body are dying and being replaced. This is the nature of all conditioned things.
Every breath brings you closer to your last. Use each one wisely.
This body is already decomposing, moment by moment. Such is impermanence.
The atoms in your body will return to the elements. Nothing is permanently yours.
Your heart has beaten millions of times already. It will not beat forever.
Your body is a temporary vessel for consciousness. Do not mistake it for self.
The skeleton already dwells within you, waiting to be revealed.
You breathe 20,000 times a day. How many are mindful?
Beneath your skin, bone waits. What you call 'yourself' is merely the wrapping.
You are one blood clot away from the end. Fragility is not weakness—it is truth.
Your last meal could be any meal. Eat with awareness.
One hundred thousand heartbeats a day. Each one is borrowed time. Honor the debt.
The face in the mirror is slowly becoming unrecognizable. Who is looking?
Your body is fighting to keep you alive right now. It will eventually lose. Be grateful for now.
Time is running out. It always was. This is why practice matters now.
This moment will never return. Are you present for it?
Every second that passes is gone forever. What remains?
You will never be this young again. Right now you are the oldest you have ever been, and the youngest you will ever be.
Tomorrow is not guaranteed. Only this breath is real.
Each birthday is a countdown. Let it remind you to practice.
Your future is shrinking while your past grows. Where is the present?
The clock doesn't stop while you sleep. Neither does impermanence.
Most of your life may already be over. What remains is precious.
Your hourglass was turned over at birth. The sand that fell is gone forever.
Everyone you love will die. Either you will witness it, or they will witness yours. Love them now.
Someone will think of you for the last time. What do you want them to remember?
Within three generations, most are forgotten. What legacy of virtue will you leave?
The people you miss most are also aging toward death. Every meeting could be the last.
Everything you build will eventually crumble. The pyramids are already crumbling to sand.
Your memories will die with you. What understanding will remain?
Your voice will eventually exist only in fading memories. Speak truth now.
The last person who remembers you will also die. What ripples will you leave?
Your childhood home will be demolished or inhabited by strangers. Nothing you know will last.
Your name will be spoken for the last time someday. What will it have meant?
What are you waiting for? Death does not wait.
Is this how you want to spend your remaining time?
Are you living or merely existing?
The things you postpone may never happen. Act now.
Your excuses die with you. Your actions live on.
Fear is a waste of limited time. Practice is not.
Every 'someday' is a day closer to never.
Wasted time cannot be recovered. This moment can be reclaimed.
Regret weighs more than risk. What are you not doing that you should?
Comfort zones are beautifully furnished coffins. Step out while you still can.
Death is not an event in life: we do not live to experience death.
Birth and death are one continuous process. Understand this and be free.
You are not promised another breath. How will you use this one?
Existence is temporary. Use it to awaken to what lies beyond change.
You have been dying since the moment you were born. This is not tragedy—it is the path.
Comfort is the enemy of awareness. Death awareness is the friend of liberation.
Permanence is an illusion. Seeing through it is wisdom.
Let the awareness of death illuminate how to live.
Today is the youngest day of the rest of your life.
Death gives no advance notice.
Your telomeres are shortening with each cell division. Time writes itself in your DNA.
Entropy is claiming your body molecule by molecule. This is the law of matter.
Your brain is slowly shrinking with age. Use it for what matters.
Every time your DNA is copied, errors can occur. Most are repaired; some remain. Imperfection is the nature of form.
Neurons die throughout your life. What have they witnessed?
The universe existed for 13.8 billion years before you. It will continue after. What will you do with your flash of consciousness?
In cosmic terms, your entire life is shorter than a camera flash. Make it illuminate something.
You are a temporary arrangement of matter that learned to contemplate itself.
Stars will burn out long after everyone forgets your name. Let your actions plant seeds that outlast you.
You are stardust that briefly learned to be afraid of returning to dust.
Men do not care how nobly they live, but only how long, although it is within the reach of every man to live nobly, but within no man's power to live long.
I wasted time, and now doth time waste me.
We are such stuff as dreams are made on, and our little life is rounded with a sleep.
Whenever his last day shall come, the wise man will not hesitate to go to meet death with steady step.
Any man's death diminishes me, because I am involved in mankind; and therefore never send to know for whom the bell tolls; it tolls for thee.
While we are postponing, life speeds by.
Human life between heaven and earth is like a white colt passing a crack in the wall: all at once, it is gone.
Prime years do not come twice; no day dawns again. Seize the moment—the years wait for no one.
Months and days are the travelers of eternity. The years that come and go are also voyagers.
Flowers bloom on the mountain, blooming through spring, summer, and autumn without cease.
I heard a Fly buzz — when I died —
Art is long, and Time is fleeting.
To philosophize is to learn how to die.
Tomorrow, at dawn, at the hour when the countryside whitens, I shall depart.
Whatever you see on earth is vanity.
Lord: it is time. The summer was immense.
Ripeness is all.
Gather ye rosebuds while ye may.
The boast of heraldry, the pomp of power, and all that beauty, all that wealth e'er gave, awaits alike the inevitable hour.
But at my back I always hear Time's wingèd chariot hurrying near.
The Moving Finger writes; and, having writ, moves on.
